'''Garum''' is a traditional Roman fermented fish sauce or condiment. It was used often in now-ancient Roman cuisine, as a condiment or sauce on its own, an additive to sauces, or as a seasoning. 

== Ingredients ==
* 1 sextarius (2 ⅓ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]]/546 [[Cookbook:ML|mL]]) [[Cookbook:Anchovy|anchovies]] or other fatty fish
* 3 sextarii (7 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]]/1.638 L) [[Cookbook:wine|wine]]

== Procedure ==
# Add anchovies and wine to a pot.
# [[Cookbook:Boiling|Boil]] the mixture until thick.
# [[Cookbook:Straining|Strain]] the fluid through a [[Cookbook:Sieve|sieve]], and bottle for future use.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Unit conversions to modern measures based on [[w:Ancient Roman units of measurement#Volume|Wikipedia's page on Roman measures]].
* Boiled version from [[w:Apicius|Apicius]], fermented from [[w:Geoponika|Geoponika]].

== Warnings ==

* Whether boiling or fermenting the fish sauce, the smell can be quite intense. Especially if fermenting. Be respectful of your neighbors.
